proof:
Source: parent proof step 7 (the degree-0 case of the homotopy identity; Simon 6.2.21 without the ∂T term). Fix N, β, x and the empty tuple v. Let b̃ := (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (N+1)) 0); it is C^∞ (β.property.1.1), hence differentiable.
1. Coordinates. By sibling coords (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_coords N), take L with L(s, y) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons s (WithLp.ofLp y)) and L(1, 0) = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. Rewrite the goal right-to-left with these identities, so that ι(s, x) = L(s, x), e₀ = L(1, 0), and the empty tuple J ∘ v becomes w := (i ↦ L(0, v_i)) : Fin 0 → ℝ^{N+1}.
2. Derivatives. y ↦ b̃(y)(w) is b̃ followed by the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ _ ℝ w, so it has derivative (apply w) ∘ Db̃(y) at y. s ↦ L(s, x) has derivative L(1, 0): compose (hasDerivAt_id s).prodMk (hasDerivAt_const s x) with L. Hence φ(s) := b̃(L(s, x))(w) has derivative ((apply w) ∘ Db̃(L(s, x)))(L(1, 0)) at every s (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt).
3. Pointwise identity. By exteriorDerivative_apply with n = 0 (b̃ is differentiable at L(s, x)):
 db̃(L(s, x))(Fin.cons L(1, 0) w) = Σ_{i : Fin 1} (−1)^i • D[y ↦ b̃(y)(i.removeNth (Fin.cons L(1, 0) w))](L(s, x))((Fin.cons L(1, 0) w) i).
 The sum has only the index 0 (Fin.sum_univ_one), (−1)^0 = 1, and removeNth 0 (Fin.cons L(1, 0) w) = Fin.tail (Fin.cons L(1, 0) w) = w (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons). So the integrand is D[y ↦ b̃(y)(w)](L(s, x))(L(1, 0)). By step 2 (HasFDerivAt.fderiv, HasDerivAt.deriv) this equals ((apply w) ∘ Db̃(L(s, x)))(L(1, 0)) = deriv φ s.
4. FTC. φ is C^∞ (apply w ∘ b̃ ∘ L ∘ (s ↦ (s, x))), so deriv φ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_deriv), hence interval integrable, and φ is differentiable everywhere. By step 3 and intervalIntegral.integral_congr, followed by intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub:
 ∫_0^1 db̃(L(t, x))(Fin.cons L(1, 0) w) dt = ∫_0^1 deriv φ = φ(1) − φ(0) = b̃(L(1, x))(w) − b̃(L(0, x))(w).
 This is (d). □

exteriorDerivative_apply with n = 0 has the single index 0, and removeNth 0 (Fin.cons e₀ w) = w, so the integrand is D[y ↦ β(y)(w)](ι(t, x))(e₀).
By the chain rule this equals deriv φ t for φ(s) = β(ι(s, x))(w), and φ is C^∞.
